title: Cubical diagonal compares multiplication evaluation roofs
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $r\geq0$, and put $D=\mathbf Z^r$, $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal A_R(D)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $t:\mathcal M\to\mathcal E$ for trivial action and $\Gamma$ for invariants [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Use ordinary derived categories and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For equivariant cochain complexes use the finite Koszul complex of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] and its total $K(P)^n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}K_R(P^b;T)^a$, with differential $d_K+(-1)^a d_P$. Let $B$ be a flat commutative equivariant $R$-algebra as in [lem-sfb-lattice-flat-twisted-chain-pairing], with the explicitly specified complex $K_B$, chain map $\star$ and unit $u$. Use $L,\varepsilon,E_B$ and $c_a$ of [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-augmentation-evaluation]. Extend the integral diagonal of [lem-sfb-integral-cubical-chain-diagonal] $R$-linearly:
$$\Delta[v,I]=\sum_{A\sqcup C=I}\epsilon(A,C)[v,A]\otimes[v+u_A,C],\qquad u_A=\sum_{i\in A}u_i.$$
It is an equivariant counital chain map $L\to L\otimes_R L$. With the signed total tensor and its associators let $\tau$ interchange the middle $tK_B$ and $L$ in $tK_B\otimes tK_B\otimes L\otimes L$; the sign on degrees $q,-p$ is $(-1)^{pq}$. Then the following are equal as chain maps from $t(K_B\otimes_R K_B)\otimes_R L$ to $B$:
$$E_B\circ(t\star\otimes1)=m_B\circ(E_B\otimes E_B)\circ\tau\circ(1\otimes\Delta).$$
For homogeneous components $x_A,y_C$ of degrees $p,q$ both sides vanish unless $A\sqcup C=I$ and otherwise have coefficient
$$c_{p+q}\epsilon(A,C)T^v(x_A)T^{v+u_A}(y_C).$$
This includes the sign identity $c_{p+q}=(-1)^{pq}c_pc_q$. Moreover $(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta=\varepsilon$ identifies the augmentation denominators of the corresponding two evaluation roofs, so their equality holds in the ordinary derived category with the ordinary K-flat tensor representatives. The unit equation is
$$E_B\circ(tu\otimes1)=\eta_B\circ\varepsilon,$$
where $\eta_B:tR[0]\to B$ is the original algebra unit. For $r=0$ these maps reduce to multiplication and unit; for $r=1$ the diagonal is $[v,\varnothing]\otimes[v,\{1\}]+[v,\{1\}]\otimes[v+u_1,\varnothing]$, and the products are $x^0\star y^1=x^0y^1$, $x^1\star y^0=x^1T_1(y^0)$. No division, characteristic restriction or nonzero-ring assumption enters these identities.

proof.text: Obtain the cell-normalized augmentation, diagonal and evaluation and the three counit identities from the normalized-roof construction. No data are defined by choosing from a mere existence assertion.

Apply the finite numerator comparison to this normalized roof and P. This supplies the multiplication and unit equations and the first supported coefficient. Rewrite the second numerator by the chain-map multiplication equation to obtain the identical supported coefficient.

Obtain the common denominator, its two quasi-isomorphisms and the K-flat tensor representatives from the tensor-representative theorem. Map the denominator and numerator equalities into the localization. Since Q(a) and Q(b) are invertible, cancel Q(a) to prove inv(Q(a));Q(f)=inv(Q(b));Q(g). This cancellation is proved explicitly in Lean for any functor which inverts the two denominators.

Prove the triangular-number identity over natural numbers using evenness of n(n+1). Applying pow_add and rearranging powers of -1 proves c_(p+q)=(-1)^(pq)c_p c_q. For rank zero and rank one simplify P.coordinates and P.unitCoordinates: empty products act by identity, singleton products by the generator. For a singleton cube, its powerset is {empty,singleton}; expanding the normalized diagonal gives precisely the two rank-one terms, because the empty and singleton partition signs are one. Assemble the unchanged conjunction.
